items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: Vincent Augberry, who is still a very dear friend of mine now -- in New York, we hang out together.

ctx.x: And we had Palamiris -- he was the alto saxophone player; George McCaskel played alto and George Kelly played tenor. And the guitar player was George Tucker and I was -- well, before I came on there, the drummer was Vincent Augberry, who is still a very dear friend of mine now -- in New York, we hang out together.

But after playing at the barbecue stand for almost a year, and hearing the guys out there at the school talk about this band that was playing up at the Elk's Rest, and they heard about me playing at the barbecue stand, Vincent Augberry was leaving the band to go and join Hartley Toots as a front man, because he could dance and snake hip and all that stuff -- and plus he was a tall, handsome fellow, so he was going to front Hartley Toots. In other words, that was big time for him, so they asked me to join the band.
